standard: Subscription / SaaS efficiency, valuation & unit-economics benchmarks corpus
source: SaaS Capital / Bessemer / KeyBanc / OpenView / ChartMogul references (web-researched 2026-07-24)

entries.title: Rule of 40 — growth rate + profit margin ≥ 40%
entries.body: Rule of 40: annual revenue growth rate (%) + profit margin (%) should equal or exceed 40%. A company growing 60% at −20% margin scores 40 (healthy growth-stage); growing 10% at 30% margin also scores 40 (healthy mature). Coined by Brad Feld 2015, popularized by Bessemer.

entries.title: Rule of 40 benchmarks (SaaS Capital Index 2024)
entries.body: SaaS Capital Index averaged a Rule of 40 score of 31 in 2024, top quartile above 50. Private growth-stage targets: Seed/Series A 60+, Series B/C 50, Series D+ 40, public 40+. Below 20 signals fundamental issues and multiple compression.

entries.title: Bessemer Rule of X — (Growth × 2) + FCF Margin
entries.body: Bessemer's Rule of X weights growth twice: (Growth Rate × 2) + FCF Margin. A 1% growth increase moves a public cloud company's valuation multiple ~2.3× as much as a 1% FCF-margin increase, because growth compounds while margin gains are linear.

entries.title: LTV — Lifetime Value (gross-margin-adjusted)
entries.body: Basic LTV = ARPA ÷ monthly churn rate. More precisely, gross-margin-adjusted LTV = (ARPA × gross margin %) ÷ monthly churn rate. Using ARR/churn without margin overstates value; margin-adjusted LTV is the figure that matters for unit economics.

entries.title: LTV:CAC ratio — 3:1 healthy, 4:1+ strong
entries.body: Median LTV:CAC ~3.6:1; 4:1+ is strong and 6:1+ top-tier (Benchmarkit 2024 / KeyBanc). Below 3:1 the business destroys value on acquisition; LTV:CAC is the counterweight to CAC and the core unit-economics test.

entries.title: CAC — Customer Acquisition Cost
entries.body: CAC = total sales & marketing expense ÷ number of new customers acquired in the same period. Include S&M salaries in the numerator; count only net-new logos (not expansion) in the denominator; account for the lag between spend and close.

entries.title: CAC payback — 12–18 months healthy, <12 strong
entries.body: Healthy B2B SaaS CAC payback is 12–18 months; under 12 months is strong; above 24 months suggests acquisition costs too high or LTV too low. Including expansion revenue in LTV shortens payback significantly (expansion costs ~half of net-new acquisition).

entries.title: Magic Number — sales efficiency
entries.body: Gross Magic Number = net-new ARR (from sales/marketing) in a quarter ÷ prior-quarter S&M spend. ~0.75+ is efficient; KeyBanc 2024 private median ~0.64, expected to reach 0.82 by 2026. Below 0.5 signals inefficient go-to-market.

entries.title: SaaS Capital Index — median ARR multiple 3.2x (2026)
entries.body: The SaaS Capital Index (equal-weighted median EV/ARR across public pure-play B2B SaaS, published monthly since 2008) read 3.2x as of 30 Jun 2026 — lowest since 2011. Multiples scale with growth: 20–30% growth ≈ 5.5x, 10–20% ≈ 3.1x, <10% ≈ 1.9x.

entries.title: Gross margin benchmark — ~77% median, 80%+ strong
entries.body: Median SaaS gross margin ~77% (Benchmarkit 2025); 80%+ is strong and 85%+ top-tier. Gross margin feeds both LTV and Rule of 40, so it is a foundational input to the whole metrics stack, not a side number.

entries.title: Burn Multiple — net cash burned ÷ net new ARR
entries.body: Burn Multiple = net cash burned ÷ net new ARR added. Below 1.0x is elite; ~1.4x growth-stage; 2.5–3.4x seed/Series A. It is the sharper early-stage efficiency test than Rule of 40, which breaks below ~$30M revenue (only ~9% of sub-$30M private SaaS pass Rule of 40).
